CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 6
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance as appropriate.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.

Article 3
The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women against gender-based violence, and to uphold the best interests of the child, in cases occurring in the household or in the public sphere.

Article 7
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions. (2) Protection of women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of Sumenep Regency, whether the violence is committed in Sumenep or outside Sumenep.
(3) Protection of women and children victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of Sumenep as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of Sumenep where the violence is committed within the territory of Sumenep Regency.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the fundamental rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 8
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics free of charge.
(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.

CHAPTER IV
HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner under P2TP2A.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, P2TP2A, in its implementation, may establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.
(3) The implementation of protection for victims as referred to in paragraph (1) must take into account religious norms as well as the rights and obligations of parents, guardians, husbands/other persons who are legally responsible for the victim.
(4) The mechanism for handling protection as referred to in paragraph (1) is stipulated by a Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER III
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND
CHILD VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE
Article 4
(1) The Regent through Regional Apparatus shall establish a public service work unit that functions as P2TP2A.
(2) The Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (1) in implementing the Protection of Women and Child Victims of Violence may coordinate with other Regional Apparatus.

HANDLING AND MECHANISM
Article 5
(1) The implementation of Protection for victims is carried out in an integrated manner under P2TP2A.
(2) In handling medical, legal, medicolegal, psychological, and economic protection, P2TP2A, in its implementation, may establish partnerships with social community institutions engaged in the field of protection of women and children.

CHAPTER II
PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES
Article 2
Protection of Women and Children Victims of Violence is carried out based on respect and recognition of equal rights and human dignity, non-discrimination, gender equality and justice as well as protection of the fundamental rights of women and children and the best interests of the victim.

Article 8
(1) Forms of protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence consist of medical, legal, medicolegal (forensic medicine), economic and psychological protection.
(2) The form of medical protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of treatment and recovery of physical injuries aimed at restoring the physical condition of victims carried out by medical personnel and paramedics free of charge.
(3) The form of legal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services and assistance to help victims undergo legal and judicial processes.
(4) The form of medicolegal protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of medical services for evidentiary purposes in the legal field.
(5) The form of economic protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of services for skills and providing economic access so that victims can be independent.
(6) The form of psychological protection for Women and Child Victims of Violence as referred to in paragraph (1) consists of assistance in order to restore the traumatic condition of victims including the provision of safe houses to protect victims from various threats and intimidation for victims and providing psychological support so that victims have self-confidence, strength and independence in resolving problems.

CHAPTER V
FORMS OF VIOLENCE AND PROTECTION
Article 6
(1) Forms of violence against Women and Children include physical, sexual, economic and psychological.
(2) Forms of physical violence are any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, unconsciousness and/or causes death.
(3) Forms of sexual violence are sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Forms of economic violence are neglect of family members in the form of not providing livelihood, care or maintenance as appropriate.
(5) Forms of psychological violence are acts that result in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or severe psychological suffering in a person.

Article 7
(1) Every woman and child who becomes a victim of violence must receive protection in accordance with applicable provisions. (2) Protection of women and children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be provided to residents of Sumenep Regency, whether the violence is committed in Sumenep or outside Sumenep.
(3) Protection of women and children victims of violence, in addition to being provided to residents of Sumenep as referred to in paragraph (2), shall also be provided to non-residents of Sumenep where the violence is committed within the territory of Sumenep Regency.

Article 3
The implementation of Protection for Women and Children Victims of Violence aims to provide protection and services to women against gender-based violence, and to uphold the best interests of the child, in cases occurring in the household or in the public sphere.
